hedges.reason: This covers the hike leg of the primary's failure (C4 or C5 YES). If inflation re-accelerates, for example through an energy or tariff shock, enough to force a July hike, then a 'Fed rate hike by [later meeting]' contract resolves YES. It pays in exactly the worlds where my C4 NO and C5 NO lose.

The hedge thesis says weak US labor data pulls easing expectations forward, lowering real yields and weakening the dollar, and gold rallies. Gold reaching the nearer rungs by end of June is the most direct listed expression of markets pricing a cut, which is the worlds where C3 YES fails. The link is loose because this market closes before the July meeting.

A marked slowdown in US growth, the path to a July cut, tends to pull crude lower through weaker demand. Lower oil also takes pressure off headline inflation, which gives the committee room to cut. So an oil dip goes with the C2 world in which the no-change basket fails.

claims.reason: This holds by construction. A 25 bp hike announced at the July 2026 meeting is an increase in the upper bound after December 16, 2025 and before any later listed meeting. So every E8 rung from July onward, including the latest and mildest one, must resolve YES.
The same logic applies. A hike of 50 bp or more at the July meeting satisfies E8's rule for the July rung and every later rung.
